notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/bottomnav.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/bottomnav.md at 31f1c5e (“docs: add onboarding home page, component search, and favicon”, 29 September), the same files on main and docs-next; the guide and evidence were written at 49baedf (28 September), and 31f1c5e only moved the summary into the guide's registration. The separate Bottom Nav Item guide (bottomnavitem) has no entry and is not cited; its evidence was read for context only. The guide's Sources note and the evidence were checked on 28 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60, so items citing them carry 2026-09-28 and 0.1.60 and the trace check flags them; the mirror has no 0.1.60 tag, so no GitHub compare to the installed build is possible. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Builds compared by blob SHA (GitHub contents API): BottomNav.tsx (756ff5a) and BottomNavItem.tsx (9e1bb31) are the same blobs at v0.1.77, v0.1.78, v0.1.78-636f3f5, -c7d3348, -a116616 and -dbe0e02, and match the installed files; the design-tokens JSON is 0582bb0 at v0.1.77 and v0.1.78 and 4545aec from 636f3f5 (8 October) to dbe0e02 (the installed file); GitHub's compare shows no patch for it (too large), so its values were read on the installed build only; figma-variables-resolver.ts (d03e77c) and typography.ts (cbabe67) are unchanged from v0.1.77; web-platform-utils.ts (c3fdb83 → e33b52b) and Icon.tsx changed and were read as installed. Every sentence quoted here was read against the installed source (read, not rendered), with token values through the package's own getVariableByName (lib/commonjs). Bar: position absolute at bottom 0, left 0 and right 0 of its nearest positioned parent, a row with alignItems center (BottomNav.tsx 63–79); bottomNav/padding/top 10, /bottom 23 and /horizontal 16, bottomNav/gap 0, a bottomNav/border/width 1 top border in bottomNav/border/color rgb(204, 207, 209) and bottomNav/background rgb(255, 255, 255) in Light and with no modes: the values the evidence quotes. Children: each element child is cloned with the bar's modes, then its own, then BottomNavItem / State Active when its value equals value and Idle otherwise (99–111), so a value matching no item leaves every item Idle and the bar keeps no state of its own; with an onPress that calls onChange with the item's value, then the item's own onPress (113–119); with accessibilityState selected (121–125); and with flex 1 before the item's own style (128), so the items share the bar equally. Items: a bottomNavItem/icon/size 24 icon over the label (11/14, weight 500, JioType Var) with a 6 px gap (BottomNavItem.tsx 61–94, 173–190), so an item is 44 px tall and the bar 1 + 10 + 44 + 23 = 78 px, as Sizing says; the label has no line limit, so a long label wraps and makes its item taller (182–188); the label defaults to “Home” and the icon to ic_home (111–112). Light colours: Idle icon rgb(48, 51, 56) and label rgb(36, 38, 43); Active icon rgb(173, 132, 68) (the accent colour) and label rgb(13, 13, 15), as the evidence says. Disabled sets opacity 0.5 (81) and the Pressable's disabled (260); on the web it sets tabIndex −1 and drops the key handler (web-platform-utils.ts 115–121, 283–291), and React Native Web 0.21.2's Pressable sets aria-disabled. Accessibility as installed: BottomNav discards accessibilityLabel (48) and gives the row role tablist with no label (84–85); each item is role tab with aria-label accessibilityLabel or label on the web (BottomNavItem.tsx 158–166, 250–252, 269; web-platform-utils.ts 188–201); React Native Web 0.21.2 reads no accessibilityState (createDOMProps takes aria-selected or accessibilitySelected only), so the Active tab gets no aria-selected. Per the team's lessons, the unnamed tab list and the missing selected state are screen-reader exposure, so they are recorded under accessibility and not as Coin gaps. Not quoted, and not flagged: the Sources sentence on why the guide stays in Light mode and the evidence’s Dark-mode Limits line. Dark mode isn’t covered by Coin yet (the brand team owns it), so by the Documentation flow’s note and the pack’s lessons it gets no flag or ticket here. Left out, and why: the Sources note's “Declared, installed, and registry jfs-components versions are 0.1.60.” (the check's version) and “Item details are in the Bottom Nav Item guide.” (a pointer to a guide with no entry); the Sizing title “Full width, fixed height” (the height stays fixed only while every label fits on one line: Content's long label makes the bar taller) and its “358 × 78” mark (the guide kit frame's 1 px border, per the evidence's Verification); the Configuration cards' widths, kept only in example 1's purpose (they hold for the guide's 360 px frame, 328 px shared: 109.3, 82 and 65.6 px; six give 54.7); the Anatomy padding mark; the evidence's Figma node, bound variables and Storybook story list, its Contract split (designer, system and developer settings), its rendered measurements other than those cited, and its Verification notes; Color Mode (building rules), style, accessibilityHint (passed to the row, line 86) and the View props such as testID, which no guide sentence covers; and the playground. Facts: the package's facts list BottomNav.Item with its own prop value only (the rest are BottomNavItem's props, which have no entry), so the evidence fact on BottomNav.Item records the item props the guide uses (value, label, iconName, disabled, onPress); they hold on dbe0e02 (BottomNav.tsx 137–147, BottomNavItem.tsx 21–38). Modes: the facts list Color Mode only; BottomNavItem / State is set by the bar from value, not chosen. Strength: “always at the bottom” is everywhere (every bar positions itself, BottomNav.tsx 63–67); “Bottom Nav only reports which destination was pressed” is contextual (it is about the Active value). Anatomy required: the Bar and each item's Label are always drawn; an Active item only when value matches a destination, and an Idle item only beside another. avoidWhen keeps the Don't's sixth destination; the guide names no other component to use instead. Content good keeps the guide's five labels; bad keeps its long label. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every Bottom Nav and Text), no modes, no style. The In context example puts the bar in a Screen, which stands in for the guide's ScreenFrame (Screen is a View with flex 1, so it is the bar's positioned parent), with a VStack of the two Texts the guide's own screen shows above it; the literal value and the empty onChange stand for the app's state, which the guide says the app keeps. The other two are the guide's 3 destinations card and its Disabled destination card (Pay disabled, Home Active). The destinations and icon names are the guide's (all five icons are in the installed icon registry). Screen, VStack and Text have entries (Screen and Text undocumented). Gaps: the Sources note's Figma and package bar heights (77 and 78 px; the evidence puts it down to the top border, drawn inside the bar in the package). Sorting (batch 13, one cross-check run): no flags. Its notes, not flags: /configuration/6's “onChange receives that destination's value” and /configuration/7's “set disabled on its BottomNav.Item” go beyond the quoted sentences but rest on the evidence's Contract (onChange(value), BottomNav.Item's props) and the installed source (BottomNav.tsx 114–119, 137–147); /accessibility/0 and /placementAdvice/2–3 describe behaviour rather than advice, which is left as it is. Left: the seven 0.1.60 trace-check flags (all still true on dbe0e02 as read here). No human flag: nothing the entry quotes is contradicted on dbe0e02.

examples.purpose: Switching sections of the app, the guide's In context: a Screen holds the Active section's content and the Bottom Nav, which anchors to its bottom edge. Five destinations, each a short noun with its own icon; Home is Active. The app keeps the Active value and swaps the content above when onChange reports a pressed destination: the literal value and the empty onChange stand for the app's own state.
examples.jsx:
<Screen>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Home" />
    <Text text="Your balances and recent activity" />
  </VStack>
  <BottomNav value="home" onChange={(value) => {}}>
    <BottomNav.Item value="home" label="Home" iconName="ic_home" />
    <BottomNav.Item value="finances" label="Finances" iconName="ic_rupee" />
    <BottomNav.Item value="pay" label="Pay" iconName="ic_scan_qr_code" />
    <BottomNav.Item value="invest" label="Invest" iconName="ic_rupee_coin" />
    <BottomNav.Item value="explore" label="Explore" iconName="ic_search" />
  </BottomNav>
</Screen>
